No.1433/2023, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant.
2. Accordingly, I.A. No.1433/2023 is dismissed as withdrawn.
3. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the case is heard finally.

4. This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of judgment dated 23/11/2022 passed by learned Third Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Devsar, District Singrauli (M.P.) in Special Case No.25/2020, whereby appellant Satya Narayan Singh Gond has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:619 2 CRA-1126-2023 convicted and sentenced as under :-

 with Section 6 Imprisonment  5.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that victim was a consenting adult and therefore a consensual relationship between two adults will not fall within the definition of rape or penetrative sexual assault as defined in Section 375 of IPC or under Section 3/5 of POCSO Act.

Thus, it is submitted that a consensual relationship between two consenting adults is not an incidence of rape and the conviction as has been recorded by the trial Court, therefore, forthwith conviction and sentence are required to be set aside and be set aside.
6. Reading from the evidence of sister of victim (PW-1), it is pointed out that sister of the victim has admitted in para-6 of her cross-examination that they are seven sisters and brothers, victim died.
There was an elder sister to the deceased, who died during her childhood.
She stated that victim was the eldest surviving daughter and thereafter this witness was born and thereafter other children were born.
This witness was asked as to what was her age, then she remained silent and did not reply even on consistent query.
7. P.W.-2 is the mother of the victim.

She has stated that the age of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:619 3 CRA-1126-2023 victim was 16 years at the time of the incident and her husband got her admitted in Class-I at Govt. Primary School Chachardol.
However, in cross- examination this witness stated that victim had studied up to 8th Class.
She had taken admission in 9th Class, but had dropped out of the school for last two-three years.
In para-8 this witness has stated that no birth certificate for the victim was prepared.
Her marriage was performed when she was 20 years of age and then she stated that at present her age was 40-45 years.
She has admitted that at the time of admission in the school age of the victim was 8-9 years.
In para-10 this witness has stated that she does not know as to in which year victim was born.
She stated that she does not know even the date of birth of the victim.

8. P.W.-3 father of the victim stated that he has seven children and then after stating that at the time of the incident age of victim was 16 years and she was pregnant of five months when Panchayat was convened where Satya Nayaran Singh Gond had denied violation of privacy of the victim.
He admits in para-7 that birth certificate has not been prepared either for himself or for any of his children.
Thereafter, in para-9 he stated that victim was second child, there was a daughter elder to the victim who died during her childhood.
9. P.W.-4 lady doctor i.e. Dr. Manju Singh stated that victim has given birth to a full term man child.
When she had examined the victim, her condition was normal.

sentences.text:
10. Mahendra Singh (P.W.-8) stated that he was working as NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:619 4 CRA-1126-2023 Government Primary Teacher at Govt. School from 2007 to 2019.

He had produced original scholar register from 01.07.2004 to 10.06.2020 on which at Sl.
No.102 name of the victim is mentioned.
This entry as contained in Ex.P-6 reveals that victim had taken admission on 01.07.2007 and her date of birth is mentioned as 02.04.2001.

However, it is pointed out that there is overwriting in the year in which victim had taken admission and also in the year in which she was studying in 2nd Class, therefore, it is pointed out that this school record being tampered is not a reliable piece of evidence.
11.
This school teacher has admitted that no birth certificate was produced along with the admission form.

12. Thus, it is submitted that its a case where victim who was an adult entered into a relationship with the appellant on her own volition and then that has been converted into a case of rape.
13.
It is also pointed out that P.W.-3 father of the victim had admitted that when he was 12-13 years of age that time his marriage was performed.
Gauna was performed after two years of his marriage i.e. at about 15 years of age and since then his wife was staying with him.
This witness stated that he does not remember as to after how many years of their Gauna victim was born, but stated that victim was the eldest child.

14. Shri Arvind Singh, learned Government Advocate for the respondent-State, in his turn, supports the impugned judgment and submits that DNA report Ex.P-28 is positive, it shows that the product of conception is biologically fathered by the appellant, therefore, no indulgence is called NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:619 5 CRA-1126-2023 for.
15.
Complaint/FIR Ex.P-8 was recorded by the victim.
In the complaint, it is mentioned that she was in friendship with the appellant Satya Narayan Singh Gond.

It is mentioned that on 02.10.2017,
Satya Narayan Singh Gond had violated her privacy and thereafter whenever he used to get an opportunity, he used to indulge in physical relationship.
As a result of said relationship, she became pregnant.
When victim had informed this fact to Satya Narayan, then he had stated that he will keep her.
As a result of which, victim had not propagated the information any further.

In the month of Falgun i.e. somewhere in February-March, she had informed about her pregnancy to her mother and then on 08.07.2018 she was admitted in a hospital at Sidhi, where she gave birth to a child.

Thus, it is evident that when victim herself had informed her mother in the month of Falgun about her privacy being violated and that matter being not reported to the police, there exists an element of consent.
Now, we are conscious of the fact that consent can be given only by a consenting adult and not by a minor.
In the eyes of law any consent given by minor has no meaning and it cannot be taken to be a valid consent.
16. When this aspect is examined, it is evident that on the Dakhil Kharij Register Ex.P/6-C, there is overwriting in the year of admission.
In Dakhil Kharij Register Ex.P/6-C, it is mentioned that victim had passed 5th Class on 01.07.2011.
Date of birth is mentioned as 02.04.2001.

sentences.text:
However, P.W.-2 mother of the victim has stated that when victim NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:619 6 CRA-1126-2023 was admitted in the school in Class-I, at that time, her age was 8-9 years.

Thus, it is evident that at the time of admission in the year 2007, if victim is treated to be 8 years of age, then her date of birth will be 02.04.1999.
18.
P.W.-1 sister of the victim has admitted that there was a elder sister to the victim who died during her childhood.
Thus, admittedly victim is second child of her parents.
19. P.W.-2 has admitted that her marriage was performed when she was 20 years of age.

This is contrary to the statement of her husband (PW-3) who has stated that when his marriage was performed, at that time, her age was 12-13 years and after two years her Gauna was performed and since then he was residing with his wife.
20.
When P.W.-1 was asked to give her date of birth in her cross- examination, she remained quite and did not reply despite asking again and again.

The father of the victim (PW-3) has stated that victim was minor, but fact of the matter is that even he could not give date of birth certificate of the victim nor any explanation for not preparing the birth certificate as is admitted by P.W.-2 also.

Thus, when statements of PW-2 are taken into consideration along with evidence of PW-8 school teacher, it is evident that at the time of admission victim was about 8 years of age, it will push her date of birth to 1999, she was a consenting adult when her privacy was violated in October, 2017,
and therefore, a consensual relationship as is admitted by the victim herself while recording the FIR wherein she has categorically stated that she had developed friendship with the appellant, will not fall within the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:619 7 CRA-1126-2023 definition of rape as defined under Section 375 of IPC or penetrative sexual assault or aggravated penetrative sexual assault as defined under Section 3/5 of POCSO Act, and therefore, conviction of the appellant cannot be sustained in the eyes of law and is hereby set aside.

21. Before we part with the judgment, it will be important to mention that despite the fact that victim had recorded the FIR as contained in Ex.P-8, no statement of her either under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. or under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. have been recorded.

Though, it has come on record that FIR was recorded in the hospital on 11.07.2018, whereas she died on 24.07.2018 and lady doctor i.e. Dr.
Manju Singh (PW-4) has stated that after delivery, her condition was normal and she had examined the victim.
22. Accordingly, this criminal appeal is allowed.
Impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence is hereby set aside and the appellant is acquitted of all the charges.
Appellant is in jail, he be released immediately, if not required in any other case.
23. Record of the trial Court be sent back immediately.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) (RATNESH CHANDRA SIN  JUDGE JUDGE  sp/-
